why: New behavioral node corpus/spec-floor — the harness that runs the project-spec-tier engines across the corpus, specified for the first time (the engine shipped ungoverned by any node). 22 boolean scenarios over four groups. Cold sdd-spec-judge ALIGNED true, oracle/builder/architect all PASS on round 5, after four rounds that each found real defects and were each fixed at the rule rather than the instance: a governance pre-flight block that was a genuine omission of five bars, two Given-format violations, an unargued near-duplicate, one regression of the mission's own round-2 remediation (a decision carried in scenario-map prose instead of drawn in the CFG) that was re-planned rather than patched again, and a dead edge where only one of the coverage guard's two conditions was exercised. The re-plan also corrected an ordering error the graph had carried since the first draft, resolving the repo root above a directory it had not yet determined. ADDITIVE: no standing scenario in any suite narrowed, rewritten or deleted, so every @frozen file self-clears untouched and no Clearance is owed. The destructive edit is at the CLI surface rather than the contract — the removal of --check-coverage from a bin-exposed script, minor at 0.2.x, declared breaking in the changeset and argued as the point of the CR rather than a side effect. Both of issue #5's triggers reproduced against main before the fix and fail the root chain after it. Grill ran past the default three-round cap; continued on a stated convergence trend rather than auto-accepting, and the overrun was reported to the owner rather than absorbed silently.
